customManagers.description: Pick up action version pins inside `vars.toml` (template root, e.g. yukimemi/pj-rust) and `.kata/vars.toml` (consumer-side, after kata seeds it from a pj-rust v0.3.1+ stack). Each pin is preceded by a `# renovate: datasource=... depName=...` annotation; the regex captures both plus the value on the next non-comment line.

Pick up `uses:` action references inside `.template` workflow files (kata sources). Renovate's default github-actions manager only scans `.yml`/`.yaml`; the `.template` suffix keeps GitHub Actions from auto-running the file in the template repo itself. This regex lets Renovate bump those `uses:` versions anyway. Fires in template repos (pj-rust-cli `release.yml.template`, pj-firebase `deploy.yml.template`, …) and is a no-op in consumer projects (their `.yml` is rendered, not `.template`).

packageRules.description: Hold every update back until the release is 3 days old. Two reasons. (1) Deno enforces its own `minimumDependencyAge` (default 24 hours) at resolve time, so a PR opened minutes after a JSR publish fails CI with "Could not find version ... that matches specified version constraint" plus a minimum-dependency-age hint — the automerge never fires and the PR sits until someone re-runs CI a day later. (2) A short quarantine is cheap supply-chain insurance across every ecosystem here (JSR, npm, crates.io, GitHub Actions): compromised or broken releases are usually yanked within hours. 3 days clears Deno's 24h window with margin for clock skew and for Renovate's own scan interval.
Auto-merge minor / patch / pin / digest bumps once CI passes. Major bumps still require human review.
Group all GitHub Actions updates into one PR (covers both the built-in github-actions manager and the regex customManager).

Consumer-side kata-managed workflow files THIS layer owns — action bumps happen UPSTREAM in `kata-apply.yml.tera` / `apm-bump.yml.tera` / `claude-review.yml.tera` / `claude.yml.tera` and flow to consumers via `kata apply`, so a Renovate-driven local bump would just be reverted on the next apply. The canonical pins live in `.kata/vars.toml` (the customManager above scans there). Each language layer disables ITS OWN rendered workflows the same way — pj-rust for `ci.yml` / `auto-tag.yml`, pj-rust-cli / pj-rust-lib / pj-rust-workspace for `release.yml`, pj-denops and pj-nvim for their `ci.yml`, pj-firebase for `deploy.yml`. pj-base must NOT list those names: it is the bottom layer and cannot know which layers compose above it, and hardcoding them here blocks projects that legitimately hand-write a file of the same name (a Lume blog on the `base` preset owning its own `ci.yml`, for instance).

The `claude_code_action` pin is kata-managed in consumer repos (back-filled into `.kata/vars.toml` via pj-base's `merge-toml, when=always` entry, unlike the consumer-owned `checkout` / `create_pull_request` pins). The canonical bump happens in pj-base's own vars.toml and flows down on the next kata apply — a consumer-side Renovate bump would be reverted by that apply, re-opened by Renovate, and so on. Disable consumer-side scanning of this one dep to break the cycle.
